sections.note: Title: Fugitive Geographies: Place, Race, and Black Education Description: How does where you grow up shape who you become? How does race determine which places are open to you, and which are not? This course takes up these questions through the lens of Black geography, examining how place and race converge to shape Black educational experience across the U.S., from cities to the rural South and beyond. We begin with foundational scholarship on space, place, and critical geographies of education, then move through paired readings that bring together academic scholarship with memoir and fiction, tracing how theoretical work on Black geographic thought and narrative accounts illuminate the same questions from different vantage points. Together these pairings ask what it means to claim, move through, and be educated within spaces not built with Black life in mind. No background in Black studies or geography is required. The course welcomes students from any discipline who want to think seriously about how place and race shape education.
sections.title: Fugitive Geographies
